key_insight: lPINN pretrains a nonlinear continuous basis offline and then solves each new PDE or inverse problem by fitting only a final linear layer while enforcing physics constraints online.
engineering_relevance: This shifts expensive representation learning out of the online loop, enabling much faster physics-constrained inference for forward and inverse modeling with better accuracy than vanilla PINNs in data-limited settings.
method: Learn operator-compatible neural basis functions from an ensemble of numerical solutions.
Pretrain the basis using solution data plus derivative information or physics residuals.
Freeze the basis for new cases and optimize only the linear output layer against PDE, boundary/initial, regularization, and observation terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors and about 1 to >100x faster online inference than vanilla PINNs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the offline training ensemble, so poor basis pretraining may limit generalization to new regimes.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
